definition: Agents share a clear common objective but fail to align behaviour to achieve it.
Mixed-motive interaction ends in an outcome off the Pareto frontier (incl. commons depletion, warfare, races to the bottom).
Undesired (often covert) cooperation between AI systems at the expense of third parties, e.g. markets or oversight schemes.
Interacting agents hold different information bearing on a joint action; private info can cause miscoordination, deception, conflict.
Small changes in node/connection properties or topology produce large changes in whole-network behaviour.
Training, deployment and replacement choices act as evolutionary forces selecting undesirable dispositions or capabilities.
Mutually adapting systems generate feedback loops, instability and unpredictability.
Difficulty forming credible commitments, trust or reputation blocks mutual gains in AI-AI and human-AI interaction.
Qualitatively new goals or capabilities emerge from composing individually innocuous systems.
Multi-agent systems create new security threats and vulnerabilities.
